subject: PulseCare — multi-year rate compact: price lock + uplift cap + renewal protection
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@pulsecare.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: PulseCare multi-year rate compact — price lock + uplift cap + renewal protection

Hi team,

Quick context: PulseCare (large payer-tech customer) is asking for a 3-year commercial arrangement that includes a fixed unit price for the first 36 months, an annual uplift cap, and a renewal-protection clause that limits surprise increases at renewal. They are pitching this as a procurement requirement for board signoff; procurement asked for explicit language in the commercial terms.

Why we should consider: strong strategic fit (platform embed across 12 hospitals), volume profile is predictable (see workbook), and they are willing to commit to an annual minimum spend that gets us closer to Dedicated-level economics.

Ask: Can Deal Desk + Finance sign off the economics and provide an exec-ready recommendation for Aditya? Specifically we need:
- Acceptable uplift cap (max %/yr) you can support
- Constraints/guardrails for renewal protection (e.g., usage variance carve-outs, feature changes)
- Any SLA exceptions or exclusions we must push back on
- An approval template (text) or conditional language we can give Procurement/legal.

Attached: PulseCare_SOW_v3.pdf (SOW draft), pricing_workbook.xlsx (usage / margin model).

Timeline: Procurement is targeting an LOA this week. I can take a call with Kimberly/Jordan at 10:30 if helpful.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0182

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@pulsecare.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T10:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: PulseCare multi-year rate compact — price lock + uplift cap + renewal protection

Laura / Jordan —

Thanks for the heads-up and the materials. Quick clarifying questions before we put together an approval package:
1) Usage mix: is the committed minimum tied to tokens, embeddings, or both? The workbook lists both — we need a single yardstick for uplift triggers.
2) Volatility floor: what historical month-to-month variance are they seeing? We need this to size the variance band for renewal protection.
3) Model variants: are they expecting us to guarantee the exact model or allow compatible-equivalent substitution? That affects the uplift allowance.

From Deal Desk perspective, initial thoughts: 36-month price lock is reasonable if the customer signs a binding minimum ARR and accepts a limited upgrade path. Uplift cap: ballpark 5–8%/yr depending on mix and hardware cost exposure. Renewal protection needs to be scoped so that significant usage deltas (>20%) can trigger reprovisioning or rate adjustments.

I'll draft two options (tight economics + strict renewal protection; looser economics + broader carve-outs) and share to escalate. Jordan — please confirm the committed ARR and the minimums we modeled.

-Kim
Kimberly Park
Director, Deal Desk

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@pulsecare.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T12:20:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: PulseCare multi-year rate compact — price lock + uplift cap + renewal protection

Kim / team —

Reviewed the workbook (attached pricing_workbook.xlsx). Summary of finance view:
- Committed ARR (as modeled): $3.2M/year average over first 3 years (min commitment clause in SOW).
- Expected blended unit cost today: $0.012/token equivalent (includes infra + amortized support).
- Minimum acceptable uplift cap: 6%/yr to preserve margin buffer if we see modest GPU pricing inflation or maintenance cost increases.

Conditions for Finance approval:
1) A binding minimum ARR with commercial remedies (recourse + minimum invoice clause).
2) Renewal protection limited to a +/- 15% usage variance band; beyond that, rates rebenchmark with a defined negotiation cadence (30–60 days).
3) Any substitution of model families during term must not increase per-token compute by >10% without prior notice.

If Deal Desk wants to push to 4% uplift cap we need a higher minimum ARR (add ~$400k/yr) or a shorter guaranteed term (24 months).

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Finance, Commercial
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@pulsecare.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T15:40:00-08:00
Subject: Escalation: Exec sign-off request (PulseCare DL-48291)

Aditya —

We need an exec decision on the commercial guardrails for PulseCare before procurement circulates LOA tomorrow. Condensed ask: approve a 36-month price lock with an annual uplift cap and narrow renewal-protection terms (see below).

Recommended deal desk package (Option A — conservative):
- 36-month price lock on current negotiated unit rates
- Uplift cap: 6% per year
- Renewal protection: +/- 15% usage variance band; beyond that, rebenchmark at 30-day cadence
- Binding Minimum ARR: $3.2M/year
- Model substitution: allowed for compatible-equivalent variants; any compute delta >10% triggers notice and reprice discussion
- Legal: add explicit carve-outs for feature deprecation and force majeure

Option B — competitive (if you want to win and smooth procurement):
- Same as A but uplift cap 4%/yr with requirement of $3.6M/year minimum ARR or an up-front prepayment covering first 6 months.

Attachments: pricing_workbook.xlsx (margin sensitivity) and a redline template for renewal protection language (included in PulseCare_SOW_v3.pdf).

We need your directional call (A or B) and any additional constraints you want on SLA or revenue recognition. If approved, Kimberly/legal will finalize text and provide exec-ready clause to give Procurement today.

Thanks —
Jordan Blake
Head, Commercial Operations

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@pulsecare.com>, procurement@pulsecare.com
Date: 2026-11-02T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Escalation: Exec sign-off request (PulseCare DL-48291)

Team / PulseCare —

Thanks for the clear package and the sensitivity analysis. I’m approving Option A with the following non-negotiable conditions to protect Redwood economics and product flexibility:

1) Term & price lock: Approved — 36 months. Price lock applies to the agreed unit rates in the attached workbook for the 36-month term.

2) Uplift cap: Approved at 6% per year. Any request to move below 6% requires a documented increase to committed ARR or prepayment as laid out in Option B.

3) Renewal protection band: +/- 15% usage variance. If usage at renewal is outside the band, we will open a 30-day rebenchmark process. During that window, current rates remain in effect; if rebenchmarking shows material delta, we reserve the right to adjust rates prospectively.

4) Model substitution & features: Legal will include language allowing Redwood to substitute compatible-equivalent model variants but requiring notice for any substitution that increases compute >10%. Feature deprecation carve-out required.

5) SLAs & exceptions: No SLA exceptions beyond standard platinum support. Any custom SLA must be separately approved and priced.

6) Binding commercial: We require the $3.2M/year minimum in the SOW with standard commercial remedies (recourse, invoice minimums).

7) Legal finalization: Kimberly + Legal — please produce an exec-ready amendment with the renewal protection clause and the uplift cap language. Once legal confirms the redline, Laura you may provide it to Procurement and request the LOA.

PulseCare — thank you, we appreciate the partnership. If Procurement needs any clarifying language for the LOA, have them loop Legal (legal@redwood.ai) and copy me.

Conditional approval provided by Aditya Rao — please ensure we capture the minimum ARR in the signed documents before any pricing is locked.

-Aditya
Aditya Rao
VP, Sales — Strategic Accounts
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
